name: Artifacts and non-parasitic mimics

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Pollen, plant cells, starch, yeast, fat droplets, air bubbles and precipitate vary widely in size and outline.
Refractile borders, budding, regular plant walls or absence of coherent parasite anatomy can guide review, but no single artifact rule is universal.

transmission.detail: Artifacts have no parasite life cycle; they originate in specimens, preparation, staining or image acquisition.

life_cycle.detail: Artifacts have no parasite life cycle; they originate in specimens, preparation, staining or image acquisition.
Background objects in stool, blood films or other preparations; record the actual specimen matrix.

hosts: No definitive or intermediate host applies.
distribution: All laboratory settings and preparation methods.
clinical_significance: Mimics cause false positives and inaccurate counts; recognizing them is an essential negative-control skill.
specimen: Background objects in stool, blood films or other preparations; record the actual specimen matrix.
diagnostics: Review focal planes, stain, calibrated size and surrounding context; seek coherent diagnostic anatomy rather than a single color or outline.
differential_diagnosis: A negative parasite classification does not identify a specific artifact.
Keep uncertain objects separate from verified artifacts; YOLO class_0 has no verified meaning here.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
